gaps.sentence: It was ___ best meal I've ever had.

gaps.explanation: 'Have an eye for something' — fixed idiom with 'an'.

gaps.sentence: ___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
gaps.explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

gaps.sentence: ___ noise pollution in cities is getting worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Noise pollution' as a general concept takes no article.

gaps.sentence: He left ___ school at sixteen and went straight into a job.
gaps.explanation: Leave school (finish education) takes no article.

gaps.sentence: She was wearing ___ old denim jacket that I loved at first sight.
gaps.explanation: 'An old…' — 'old' starts with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ good news is that sales are up by twenty per cent.
gaps.explanation: 'News' is uncountable but takes 'the' when specified: the good news is… 'Sales' here is general, so no article.
